name: Number Usage Expression
description: Examines how numbers, statistics, and figures are integrated and formatted within the text. AI models tend to present numbers in highly predictable, standardized formats (e.g., rigid adherence to AP style, excessive use of precise percentages, or artificially balanced statistical citations) and struggle to replicate the inconsistent, context-dependent way humans write numbers.
algorithm: Numeric Formatting and Statistical Precision Mapping
mechanism: This algorithm scans the text to extract all numerical expressions, analyzing their format (digits vs. spelled-out words), precision (exact metrics vs. approximations), and syntactic distribution. Large Language Models (LLMs) are aligned to present information authoritatively and clearly. Therefore, when generating text involving data, they default to highly precise, 'textbook' formatting (e.g., 'In 2023, 47.3% of the demographic...'). They rarely mix formats inconsistently in the same paragraph unless explicitly prompted. Human writers, however, are naturally inconsistent: a human might write 'three hundred people' in one sentence and '300 visitors' in the next, or use colloquial approximations like 'a couple dozen' or 'roughly half'. Furthermore, AI text often exhibits 'statistical hallucination balance'—when generating fake statistics, it tends to distribute numbers evenly (avoiding too many numbers ending in 0 or 5 to seem 'authentic', ironically creating a mathematically detectable pattern of fake randomness). The system calculates a 'Numeric Rigidity Score' by evaluating the adherence to strict formatting rules and the distribution of approximations versus exact figures.
useCase: Crucial for auditing financial reports, scientific abstracts, news articles, and any data-heavy content, distinguishing the 'perfect', sterile numerical formatting of a machine from the organic, sometimes messy reporting of a human.
strengths:
• Highly effective on data-driven or analytical texts where numbers appear frequently.
• Detects the underlying formatting rules hardcoded into the AI's alignment, which average users rarely think to alter via prompting.
• Excellent at identifying AI 'hallucinated' statistics by analyzing the underlying distribution of the generated random numbers.
limitations:
• Susceptible to false positives when analyzing highly regulated documents (like audited financial statements, deeply edited journalism, or strict APA-formatted research papers) where human writers are forced to use rigid numerical formatting.
• Less effective on creative fiction or philosophical texts where numbers are entirely absent.
• Can be bypassed by users who explicitly prompt the AI to use colloquial approximations (e.g., 'write this using rough estimates').
parameters:
Analysis: Regex Numeric Extraction and Format Profiling
Metric: Format Consistency and Precision vs. Approximation Ratio
Output: 0-100 Numeric Rigidity (Format Artificiality) Score
accuracy: Moderate — 65-75% accuracy. A highly specialized metric that provides excellent signal in data-heavy texts but should be ignored in texts lacking numerical data.

references.title: Manning, C.D. & Schütze, H. (1999). Foundations of Statistical Natural Language Processing. MIT Press.
Mitchell, E. et al. (2023). DetectGPT: Zero-Shot Machine-Generated Text Detection using Probability Curvature. ICML.
